newsitem.title: UK: Moody's rates Toyota Motor Finance issue Aaa.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates Toyota Motor Finance issue Aaa.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday it had assigned an Aaa rating to the 200 million sterling 7.5 percent eurobonds due 2001, of Toyota Motor Finance Netherlands (TMF).
TMF is a wholly owned subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation (Toyota).

"The rating is based on the support provided by Toyota for its subsidiary, which is evidenced by a keepwell agreement which states that Toyota will continue to own 100 percent of TMF, will maintain TMF's net worth above a certain minimum level, and will make available sufficient funds as requested by TMF in the event that TMF is unable to meet its payment obligations," Moody's said in a statement.
"The rating acknowledges Toyota's position as the third largest global auto manufacturer as well as the group's strong financial position," it added.
It said Toyota maintains a relatively unleveraged capital structure and high degree of financial flexibility.
It added that the rating also recognised the potential for continued pressures on earnings and cash flow due to weak domestic auto demand and adverse currency conditions.
"Toyota's core business position in Japan remains dominant, although market share over the past few years has been under pressure," Moody's said.
"The company is well established in North America, Europe and several Asia-Pacific markets where it has large sales, manufacturing and development operations."
It said the the firm's management had responded to depressed domestic demand and unfavorable currency conditions with an increased emphasis on cost reduction programmes.

"Yet, continuing currency pressures are increasing the urgency to shift additional production capacity into the local markets," Moody's said. "With weakened domestic demand and a policy of lifetime employment, Toyota will be challenged to reduce costs adequately to regain prior profitability levels.

While Moody's said that a core underpinning of Toyota's rating was its significant financial flexibility and ability to adjust to changing industry conditions, it added that should the operating challenges facing Toyota ultimately erode this flexibility, downward pressure on the long-term rating could result.
